author: codex
claim: Replace guardrails-client.sh's terminal exit 1 with an actual blocking decision.
why: Live inspection found that the <REDACTED> failure branch claims fail-closed but ends with exit 1 and no deny JSON. That is a non-blocking hook error, so infrastructure failure removes this protection precisely when bypassPermissions is active. [Hook exit semantics](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#other-exit-codes).
expected_gain: reliability: closes one deterministic fail-open path affecting every PreToolUse event
verification_command: python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; s=(Path.home()/".claude/hooks/guardrails-client.sh").read_text(); print({"claims_fail_closed":"fail-closed" in s,"terminal_statement":s.strip().splitlines()[-1]})'
risk: Unavailable guard infrastructure will block work; preserve a bounded local fallback and test failure handling before rollout.

author: codex
claim: Replace the live 3000, 8000 and 10000 hook timeouts with explicit second-scale budgets.
why: The complete settings contain timeout=3000 for guardrails, 8000 for PreCompact and 10000 for SubagentStop; hook timeout units are seconds. These permit stalls of 50, 133 and 167 minutes, respectively; guard subprocess deadlines must expire early enough to return a blocking decision before the outer timeout. [Hook timeout fields](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#common-fields).
expected_gain: latency + reliability: reduce configured worst-case stalls from hours to seconds; normal-path gain unmeasured
verification_command: python3 -c 'import json,pathlib; d=json.loads((pathlib.Path.home()/".claude/settings.json").read_text()); print([(e,g.get("matcher",""),h.get("timeout")) for e,gs in d.get("hooks",{}).items() for g in gs for h in g.get("hooks",[]) if h.get("timeout",0)>=60])'
risk: Overly short limits can interrupt handoff persistence; select budgets from measured runtimes rather than mechanically dividing every value by 1000.

author: codex
claim: Delete cc-status registrations from PreToolUse and PostToolUse while retaining lifecycle status events.
why: The inspected global-plus-project configuration matches 16 command handlers per successful Bash call, 15 per Edit/Write and 7 per Read, excluding plugin hooks and nested subprocesses. Matching handlers run concurrently, so elapsed overhead follows the slowest synchronous handler in each phase rather than the sum, but every registration still incurs execution overhead. [Hook execution](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks#hook-handler-fields).
expected_gain: cost + latency: remove 1800 handler launches in an illustrative 300-turn session averaging 3 successful tools per turn; removing 20 ms from each call's critical path would save 18 seconds
verification_command: python3 -c 'import json,pathlib,re; ds=[json.loads(p.read_text()) for p in [pathlib.Path.home()/".claude/settings.json",pathlib.Path(".claude/settings.json")]]; [print(t,{e:len({h["command"] for d in ds for g in d.get("hooks",{}).get(e,[]) if g.get("matcher","") in ("","*") or re.search(g["matcher"],t) for h in g.get("hooks",[]) if h.get("type")=="command"}) for e in ("PreToolUse","PostToolUse")})
risk: The terminal indicator loses per-tool transitions; lifecycle indicators remain available. Actual wall-clock savings require timing and may be smaller than process-count savings.

author: codex
claim: Delete the telemetry-only codex-spalla-trigger PostToolUse registration and the command-text history sink in bash_call_log.sh.
why: The spalla script launches Python three times per matching event, logs a target and suggests review; it does not dispatch a reviewer. Separately, bash_call_log.sh falls back to the original command when redaction produces no output, converting a telemetry failure into cleartext logging; retain only necessary structured metadata.
expected_gain: cost + reliability: remove 900 shell-handler launches and approximately 2700 Python launches per 900 eligible calls, plus eliminate one verified raw-command fallback
risk: Review reminders and command-history consumers lose their inputs; identify those consumers and preserve explicit review dispatch and metadata-only operational alerts.

author: codex
claim: Remove bypassPermissions as the global default and enable sandboxed execution with narrowly scoped autonomous permissions.
why: The inspected settings combine an unsandboxed shell with global bypass and broad Edit/Read/Write grants; 107 permission rules do not establish an operating-system boundary between concurrent worktrees. Use dontAsk with explicit grants for unattended lanes, and constrain filesystem and network access; hook subprocesses require separate scrutiny because they execute outside the Bash sandbox. [Sandbox boundaries](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing#protected-paths).
expected_gain: reliability: materially reduce the blast radius of an erroneous command across host configuration, sibling worktrees and remote access; incident reduction cannot be quantified from this snapshot
verification_command: python3 -c 'import json,pathlib; d=json.loads((pathlib.Path.home()/".claude/settings.json").read_text()); p=d.get("permissions",{}); print({"mode":p.get("defaultMode"),"sandbox_enabled":d.get("sandbox",{}).get("enabled"),"unqualified_file_grants":[x for x in p.get("allow",[]) if x in ("Read","Write","Edit")]})'
risk: Existing SSH, build and orchestration commands may fail until their necessary permissions are scoped correctly; enabling the Bash sandbox alone does not contain hooks or every tool.

author: codex
claim: Delete arsenal-probe launching from <REDACTED> and give nonessential startup reports explicit bounded deadlines.
why: There are seven configured startup handlers, and the digest handler can launch a detached arsenal_probe.py when its report is stale. Its existing mkdir lock prevents duplicate refreshes, but opening an editor session still owns unrelated background maintenance; use the fleet's scheduled refresh and read its cached result at startup.
expected_gain: reliability + latency: remove one background probe launch per eligible stale interval and bound report-related startup delays; current startup latency has not been measured
risk: A failed scheduled refresh leaves stale startup information; retain a visible freshness timestamp and an explicit refresh command.

author: codex
claim: Remove unconditional registrations of stop_verify.py and seam_verify.py, which immediately exit unless explicitly forced.
why: Both scripts launch Python before checking their FORCE switch. If activated, stop_verify.py treats any dirty worktree as unfinished work, lacks a stop_hook_active check, and recommends repository-wide staging or stashing; that can interfere with intentional handoffs and unrelated changes.
expected_gain: cost + reliability: remove two Python launches per Stop event and retire a latent repeated-stop and indiscriminate-cleanup failure mode
risk: An operator relying on the FORCE switches loses those checks; preserve required verification in the explicit completion workflow, scoped to the session's owned changes.

author: codex
claim: Delete the standalone context_hygiene PostToolUse registration and reuse the existing context guard's usage calculation for advisory notices.
why: context_hygiene reads and parses up to 400000 transcript bytes on every Read/Bash/Grep/Glob event; its 20-call throttle limits notices only after that work. The existing PreToolUse context guard already imports the same usage reader, so eligible calls repeat the scan and maintain an additional counter.
expected_gain: cost + latency: remove up to 900 Python launches and 360 MB of repeated transcript reading/parsing per 900 eligible calls; cached filesystem reads mean this is not necessarily physical disk traffic
risk: Removing the module itself would break the guard's import; remove only the registration and retain or relocate the useful oversized-Read warning.

author: claude
claim: sandbox.enabled=false combined with permissions.defaultMode=bypassPermissions means the harness's native OS-level Bash sandbox (filesystem/network isolation per tool call) is never invoked; isolation is done entirely by a 55-rule deny-list instead.
why: The sandbox mechanism intercepts syscalls/network at the OS layer before a command runs; a deny-list only pattern-matches the command string beforehand, so any command not anticipated by a deny rule (obfuscated, aliased, or composed via `bash -c`) runs with full host access on a bypassPermissions session.
expected_gain: reliability + capability: closes a class of deny-list-bypass exposures without adding prompts
verification_command: cat ~/.claude/settings.json .claude/settings.json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import json,sys; [print(json.loads(l).get('sandbox')) for l in sys.stdin if l.strip()]" 2>/dev/null; grep -r '"sandbox"' ~/.claude/settings.json .claude/settings*.json 2>/dev/null
risk: if sandboxing isn't actually supported for the shell/tools this fleet relies on (e.g. cron daemons needing raw network), enabling it could break automation rather than harden it

author: claude
claim: PostToolUse and PreToolUse hooks are wired against mcp__playwright__* and mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tool matchers even though playwright and claude-in-chrome (browser control) are both in mcp_disabled, so those hook entries never fire and are dead configuration.
why: Hook matchers are evaluated per tool call against the tool's registered name; a matcher referencing a tool that has no live MCP server behind it can never match, so the hook (and its script: <REDACTED>) is pure config weight with zero effect.
expected_gain: tokens + latency: trivial per-call cost removed, plus removes a false signal that browser automation is live
risk: if these MCP servers are toggled on intermittently (not always disabled), the hook is intentional dormant wiring and removing it would require re-adding later

author: claude
claim: cc-status is registered as a '*' matcher hook on Notification, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, SessionEnd, SessionStart, Stop, StopFailure, and UserPromptSubmit simultaneously, i.e. on nearly every lifecycle event rather than the one or two that actually need a status refresh.
why: Each hook firing is a subprocess spawn charged against wall-clock latency of the triggering action; the matcher field exists specifically to scope a hook to the events/tools that need it, and '*' on 8 event types forgoes that scoping entirely.
expected_gain: latency: removes redundant subprocess spawns per tool call across long 100k-400k token sessions where this repeats thousands of times
risk: if cc-status is what drives a live status line or cross-machine dashboard, trimming its triggers could make the dashboard stale on the untouched events

author: claude
claim: commit-push-pr, feature-dev, clean_gone, and receiving-code-review are all forced to skillOverrides:'user-invocable-only', which disables the harness's native automatic skill-matching (the description-based auto-trigger) for exactly the four skills a long unattended cron/daemon session would most want to fire on its own.
why: Automatic skill invocation works by matching the user/task context against each skill's description with no explicit /command; forcing user-invocable-only removes that skill from the auto-match pool, so a background agent session can only reach it via an explicit Skill call it must already know to make.
expected_gain: capability: restores autonomous self-triggering for commit/PR and code-review flows in unattended sessions
risk: if these were deliberately gated because autonomous auto-commit/auto-PR was judged unsafe on a bypassPermissions solo fleet, loosening it re-opens that risk

author: claude
claim: <REDACTED> is set as an env var, but the current Agent tool schema states team_name is deprecated and ignored because 'the session has a single implicit team', so this flag now toggles a no-op.
why: An env flag that gates a code path the runtime has since collapsed does nothing but occupy an env slot and mislead anyone reading the config into thinking multi-team agent orchestration is active.
expected_gain: capability clarity: removes a dead knob, no runtime effect either way
verification_command: claude --version; echo | claude -p 'call Agent with team_name=test and report if it errors or is ignored' 2>&1 | head -20
risk: if a specific claude_code build on one of the three machines still honors team_name, removing the flag could silently disable working multi-team behavior on that machine only

author: claude
claim: ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH is set, but only one MCP server (nuzantara-knowledge) is enabled and five others are disabled, so the deferred-tool-loading mechanism ToolSearch exists to amortize (large MCP/tool schema sets crowding the system prompt) has little surface left to defer against on this machine.
why: ToolSearch's benefit is proportional to how many tool schemas would otherwise sit fully-loaded in context; with most MCP servers already disabled, the mechanism is running against a small remaining tool set and captures a fraction of its possible token savings.
expected_gain: tokens: low-to-moderate, bounded by how many tools nuzantara-knowledge plus the 33+24 agents/skills actually expose
risk: none from measuring; but re-enabling more MCP servers to 'use ToolSearch properly' would reintroduce the exact tool-bloat ToolSearch is meant to fix, so this is informational only

author: claude
claim: Three separate PreCompact hooks (bash, <REDACTED>, python3) plus a manual CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS env override sit alongside the harness's native auto-compaction, suggesting compaction is being manually re-implemented/backed-up rather than tuned through the native summarization path.
why: PreCompact hooks fire immediately before the harness's own summarization pass; stacking three of them (one purely for transcript backup) to run at every compaction event, on top of a hardcoded token-window override, indicates the native auto-compaction's summary is not trusted as the sole record and is being defended against with manual scaffolding.
expected_gain: reliability: clarifies whether native compaction summaries are actually being relied on for continuity across the long 100k-400k token sessions this fleet runs, or whether the backup script is the rea
verification_command: grep -n 'PreCompact' -A6 ~/.claude/settings.json .claude/settings*.json 2>/dev/null; ls -la $(grep -rn '<REDACTED>' ~/.claude 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -d: -f1 | xargs dirname 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null
risk: if the backup script is the only durable record used to recover context after compaction (i.e. native summaries are treated as lossy), removing or reordering these hooks could lose session continuity on the next compaction
